reason: The cited lines show the tool querying a database connector for table schemas, row counts, comments, indexes, stored procedure details, parameters, return types, and definitions, then returning those results in the tool response. That supports SECRET because database metadata/details are brought into the agent context. It also supports UNTRUSTED because object names, comments, defaults/descriptions, and procedure definitions are database-controlled content that may be attacker-controllable. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution. They also do not show delivery of agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination; returning a tool result or issuing a fixed read-only count query to the database is not a SINK as defined.
